statement.text:
Let G be a finite group and p be a prime. Let Ψp,G be the class function
of G which vanishes on all p-singular elements of G and whose value at each p-regular
element x of G is the number of p-elements of CG (x).
    (a) Is it true that Ψp,G is a character of G?
    (b) If yes, can Ψp,G be afforded by a projective RG-module, where R is a complete
discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero such that the field of fractions of R is
a splitting field for G and its subgroups, and the residue field R/J(R) is a splitting
field of characteristic p for G and its subgroups?
     It is known that Ψp,G is a character when G ∼  = Sn for any positive integer n and
any prime p (T. Scharf, J. Algebra, 139, no. 2 (1991), 446–457).            G. Robinson
